Veteran Swedish Airmen Observe, Describe Disk-Shaped Aircraft Over Sweden  #uapx

On 17 December 1953, while flying a DC-3 over Skåne (southern Sweden), they observed an airborne object flying in the opposite direction to their aircraft.

What They Saw

Both men initially thought it might be a high-speed jet because it moved so fast and without visible exhaust.

On closer observation, they described it as:

Symmetrical and metallic, or white-shiny in appearance.

Circular or slightly elliptical in shape — resembling a “disk” or “flying lozenge.”

Roughly 10 meters in diameter (estimated)

They believed it had no visible crew and might have been some kind of unmanned device.

Estimated speed was comparable to the speed of sound and far greater than the DC-3 they were piloting.

There was no flame or smoke trail, unlike conventional aircraft.

Swedish Defence Staff acknowledged the sighting but reported no known aircraft in the area at the time.

Experts considered various explanations, with some officials suggesting it might be a daytime meteor, though this was contested.

Other theories mentioned in the press included balloons, but these were not seen as likely explanations by the primary witnesses.
